factual_claims.claim: Operating profit rose 12.2% to EUR 32.7 million, and the operating margin improved from 24.4% to 27.6%.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Operating profit increased by EUR 3.6 million (+12%) to EUR 32.7 million. The operating profit margin increased from 24.4% to 27.6%.

factual_claims.claim: Profit before income tax increased 25% to EUR 27.9 million, supported by a EUR 2.5 million reduction in net finance costs as interest rates and debt declined.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Profit before income tax was EUR 27.9 million, increasing by EUR 5.6 million (+25%) compared to 2024. Finance costs — net decreased by EUR 2.5 million (–30%) to EUR 4.8 million due to the general fall in interest rates (Euribor) and reduced loans.

factual_claims.claim: Net profit rose 17.3% to EUR 22.5 million, with earnings per share increasing from EUR 0.07 to EUR 0.09.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: The Group’s profit for 2025 was EUR 22.5 million (EUR +3.3 million, +17%). Basic and diluted earnings per share increased from EUR 0.07 to EUR 0.09.

factual_claims.claim: The increase in income tax expense, up 73.3% to EUR 5.4 million following changes to dividend taxation, limited the growth in net profit.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Income tax expense increased by EUR 2.3 million (+73%) to EUR 5.4 million. The growth was smaller as the dividend income tax expense increased in 2025 due to the rise in the tax rate and the abolition of the lower rate for regular dividends.

factual_claims.claim: The associate Green Marine contributed a EUR 26 thousand loss, compared with a EUR 487 thousand profit in 2024.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED

factual_claims.claim: Operating volumes generally recovered.

factual_claims.source_evidence: The number of passengers grew by 1.0% to 8.3 million. Cargo volume increased by 5.1% to 13.8 million tonnes. The number of cruise ship calls increased by 18 calls.

factual_claims.claim: Cargo volume increased 5.1% to 13.8 million tonnes, driven especially by a 47% increase in liquid bulk and moderate growth in dry bulk.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Cargo volume grew by 0.7 million tonnes (+5%) to 13.8 million tonnes. The largest growth was seen in liquid bulk (+0.6 million tonnes, +47%).

factual_claims.claim: Passenger numbers rose 1.0% to 8.3 million, including a 25% increase in cruise passengers; however, volumes remained approximately 78% of the pre-pandemic level.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: The number of passengers grew by 1.0% to 8.3 million. The number of cruise passengers increased by 25%. The number of passengers formed approximately 78% of the level prior to the COVID-19 pandemic.

factual_claims.claim: Domestic ferry traffic served 2.5 million passengers and 1.2 million vehicles, while Botnica’s utilisation rate fell to 49%.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: The ferries performed a total of 23,050 voyages, serving 2.5 million passengers (+1.2%) and 1.2 million vehicles (+3.5%). Botnica’s utilisation rate was 49% (–19.0%) in 2025.

factual_claims.claim: Capital investment decreased 14.4% to EUR 33.2 million, with major spending on the new multifunctional quay at Paldiski South Harbour, Muuga quay reinforcement and ferry maintenance.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: In 2025, the Group invested EUR 33.2 million, which was EUR 5.6 million, i.e. 14%, less than in the previous year. The largest investment was related to the completion of the new multifunctional quay and the 10-hectare back-up area at Paldiski South Harbour. The largest investments at Muuga Harbour were in quay reinforcement. In the Ferry segment, the main investments included the replacement of main engines on the ferry Leiger and planned dry-dock maintenance for the ferries Tiiu, Piret, and Regula.

factual_claims.claim: Net debt declined 15.5% to EUR 141.7 million, and operating cash flow increased to EUR 53.7 million from EUR 48.7 million.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Net debt at period-end was EUR 141.7 million (EUR 141,708 thousand), down EUR 25.9 million (–15.5%) from EUR 167.6 million (EUR 167,622 thousand) at 31 December 2024. Cash from operating activities was EUR 53.7 million (EUR 53,706 thousand), up from EUR 48.7 million (EUR 48,733 thousand) in 2024.

factual_claims.claim: The Group paid EUR 19.2 million in dividends, or EUR 0.073 per share.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: In 2025, we paid shareholders a dividend of EUR 0.073 per share, in the total amount of EUR 19.199 million, i.e. 100% of the previous year’s profit.

factual_claims.claim: Management expects moderate passenger and cargo growth in 2026 but anticipates pressure from higher input costs, increased financing needs and the absence of certain one-off benefits, potentially reducing operating and net profit.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: For 2026, we expect a moderate continuation of the recovery in passenger numbers. In cargo volumes, we forecast growth, but this will be affected by the general economic situation in Estonia and among our main trading partners. We see growth opportunities in revenue, but due to the increase in input prices, pressure on operating expenses is likely. Furthermore, regarding the comparison base, it must be noted that events with a one-off positive impact took place in 2025, such as the receipt of insurance indemnity and the sale of land in Muuga Harbour. Financial expenses will be affected by the increase in financing needs arising from ongoing investments. Therefore, it is likely that the Group’s operating profit and net profit may decrease.
